feedback.problem: Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}.$ If $T$ is a linear transformation such that $T(i)=i$ and $T(j)=1.5i+j,$ then what is the geometric interpretation of the transformation $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the unit square spanned by the vectors $i$ and $j.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/db15a65fd944c24ea2545baea08e6a0789b749295f623d8d4fdc2f07a37d4b73.png)

Now, using the fact that $T(i)=i$ and $T(j)=1.5i+j,$ we can draw the image of the square under the transformation $T:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/f5ebbff856529ad8cd3da41bf2f7d373294af3e0153c5e8da7da4c7b069b8b25.png)

Therefore, the linear transformation $T$ represents a horizontal shear with a shear factor of $1.5.$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: A horizontal shear with a shear factor of $1.5$
